skill: Linear Inequalities in One or Two Variables
stem: Which of the following values of \(x\) satisfies the inequality \(7x - 13 > 8\)?
explanation: Solving \(7x - 13 > 8\) gives \(7x > 21\), so \(x > 3\). Among the choices, only 4 is strictly greater than 3. The value 3 makes the two sides equal but does not satisfy the strict inequality. The value 2 results in \(7(2) - 13 = 1\), which is less than 8. The value 1 yields \(7(1) - 13 = -6\), also less than 8.

skill: Linear Inequalities in One or Two Variables
stem: A shipping company charges 9 dollars per pound plus a flat fee of 23 dollars. A customer has a budget of at most 131 dollars. Which inequality represents all possible weights \(w\), in pounds, the customer can ship?
explanation: The total cost is \(9w + 23\) dollars, and the customer can spend at most 131 dollars, so the inequality is \(9w + 23 \leq 131\). Using \(\geq\) instead of \(\leq\) reverses the budget constraint, requiring the cost to be at least 131 dollars. Swapping the coefficients to \(23w + 9\) incorrectly assigns the flat fee as the per-pound rate. Subtracting 23 instead of adding it misrepresents the flat fee as a discount.

skill: Linear Inequalities in One or Two Variables
stem: A factory produces two types of components, \(x\) and \(y\). Each unit of \(x\) requires 11 minutes of machine time, and each unit of \(y\) requires 7 minutes. The factory has at most 613 minutes of machine time available. Additionally, the factory must produce at least 17 more units of \(y\) than \(x\). If the factory wants to maximize the number of units of \(x\), what is the maximum number of units of \(x\) that can be produced?
explanation: The constraints are \(11x + 7y \leq 613\) and \(y \geq x + 17\). To maximize \(x\), set \(y\) to its minimum value: \(y = x + 17\). Substituting into the time constraint gives \(11x + 7(x + 17) \leq 613\), which simplifies to \(18x + 119 \leq 613\), so \(18x \leq 494\) and \(x \leq 27.\overline{4}\). Since \(x\) must be a whole number, the maximum is 27. Verification: \(x = 27, y = 44\) gives \(11(27) + 7(44) = 297 + 308 = 605 \leq 613\). The value 29 comes from an arithmetic error when subtracting 119 from 613. The value 24 results from incorrectly using \(y = x + 17\) in only one constraint and not minimizing \(y\). The value 34 ignores the second constraint entirely, dividing 613 by 18 and rounding incorrectly.

skill: Systems of Two Linear Equations in Two Variables
stem:
What is the value of \(x\) in the solution to the system of equations below?

\(3x + 2y = 31\)
\(x - 2y = -7\)
explanation: Adding the two equations eliminates \(y\): \((3x + 2y) + (x - 2y) = 31 + (-7)\), which gives \(4x = 24\), so \(x = 6\). Substituting back: \(3(6) + 2y = 31\) gives \(2y = 13\), so \(y = 6.5\), confirming the solution satisfies both equations.

skill: Systems of Two Linear Equations in Two Variables
stem: A bookstore sells hardcover books for 19 dollars each and paperback books for 8 dollars each. On a particular day, the store sold 37 books and collected a total of 439 dollars. How many hardcover books were sold?
explanation: Let \(h\) be the number of hardcover books and \(p\) be the number of paperback books. The system is \(h + p = 37\) and \(19h + 8p = 439\). From the first equation, \(p = 37 - h\). Substituting: \(19h + 8(37 - h) = 439\), so \(19h + 296 - 8h = 439\), giving \(11h = 143\) and \(h = 13\). The value 17 results from swapping the prices, assigning 8 dollars to hardcovers and 19 dollars to paperbacks. The value 20 comes from an arithmetic error when combining like terms. The value 11 arises from dividing 439 by 37 and rounding, ignoring the two different prices.

skill: Systems of Two Linear Equations in Two Variables
stem:
The system of equations below has no solution. What is the value of the constant \(k\)?

\(6x - 14y = 9\)
\(kx + 21y = -4\)
explanation: For a system of two linear equations to have no solution, the lines must be parallel: the ratios of the coefficients of \(x\) and \(y\) must be equal, but the ratio of the constants must differ. Setting \(\frac{6}{k} = \frac{-14}{21}\) gives \(\frac{6}{k} = -\frac{2}{3}\). Cross-multiplying: \(18 = -2k\), so \(k = -9\). Checking the constant ratio: \(\frac{9}{-4} \neq -\frac{2}{3}\), confirming no solution exists (not infinitely many solutions). The value 9 results from dropping the negative sign during cross-multiplication. The value -6 comes from incorrectly using the constant terms in the proportionality condition. The value 6 results from both ignoring the negative sign and confusing which coefficients must be proportional.
